scheme: NNN = one unique game/codebase; NNN-M = confirmed derivative/variant of the same codebase (lineage confirmed via scripts/lib_similarity_cluster.py and/or manual master.c/chinese.c/etc diffing per AGENTS.md §2.1). 9xx = non-LPC / not-convertible / deprioritized-English archives. Byte-identical duplicate archive files share their sibling's number (duplicate_of set).

libs.name: 山海战神
libs.english_name: War God of Mountains and Seas
libs.english_description: A Chinese-language adaptation of Spock's English-language science-fiction engine "Final Frontier v0.6e," part of the simple/ES II engine family. It was the very first library converted for this project, and the template most of the project's later restoration fixes were worked out on. Despite the wuxia-sounding name, it's not a martial-arts MUD but a hard-sci-fi combat simulator, with stats like Strength, Agility, and Technique and mecha- and laser-flavored battles.

libs.name: 星战英雄
libs.english_description: The game's full title is "Sands of a Turbulent World: Star War Hero," an early domestic MudOS title in the "xkx" lineage. Despite the sci-fi-sounding name, it's actually a traditional wuxia MUD built around jianghu sects and internal/external martial cultivation — "Star War" was simply a catchy name chosen by the original author, with no connection to space warfare.

libs.name: 小雨西游Ⅱ (Xiaoyu Xiyou II)
libs.english_name: Light Rain Journey to the West II (Xiaoyu Xiyou II)
libs.english_description: Originally archived under the generic filename "20150716 unknown lib.zip," this is actually a Journey to the West-themed entry in the venerable "Nitan" family of MudOS mudlibs, sharing a common lineage with this project's sibling snapshot xiaoyuxiyou. Set against the mythology of Journey to the West, it follows players through sects, magic treasures, and demons encountered along the pilgrimage route, with experience-point and potential-stat progression typical of the genre. New characters start out in worldly scenes like Chang'an's Yingxiong Restaurant, where they can take on a master, befriend fellow wanderers, and venture into demon-haunted realms; the overall tone is light-hearted and family-friendly.

libs.name: 小雨西游
libs.english_description: A Journey to the West-themed wuxia/xianxia MUD set around the Aolai Kingdom and Green Fragrance Tower, with characters, quests, and place names closely tied to the classic novel's mythology, emphasizing traditional scripture-seeking and demon-slaying character growth. It shares an identical chinese.c file with this project's xyxy2 lib, pointing to a common engine lineage, and also features a fairly complete clan system, celestial-realm announcements, and message boards.

libs.name: 书剑天下 (ShuJian MUD)
libs.english_description: A classic wuxia MUD developed and maintained since 1997 by the ShuJian MUD Wizard Group at Chongqing Telecom. New players train in a full beginner region at the martial hall, complete with a training dummy that mirrors an attacker's own stats for safe sparring, and can join any of fifteen sects either through formal apprenticeship or a built-in "gift envoy" shortcut for newcomers.

libs.name: 书剑·经典 (ShuJian Classic)
libs.english_description: A later, more complete snapshot from the same core engine as Book and Sword World (bxsj), inheriting its sect, apprenticeship, and beginner-friendly training systems; ships with multi-platform production driver binaries indicating it once ran as a live server. New characters are personally guided through the basics by an escort NPC at the martial hall.

libs.name: 金庸文字版
libs.english_description: The original package was named "Jin Yong Text Edition." Comparison confirms this is the same codebase as this project's bxsj (Book and Sword: World of Jianghu) and bxsj1 — different historical snapshots of the same wuxia MUD lineage — named after Jin Yong's novel The Book and the Sword.

libs.name: 江湖 I (Jianghu I)
libs.english_description: A large, traditional MudOS-lineage wuxia MUD, unrelated in code lineage to the "Book and Sword" series. New characters choose one of four starting temperaments in the "Land of Peach Blossoms" starting area and can receive a substantial one-time gift of skills and equipment simply by asking a wandering envoy about the jianghu — a much faster on-ramp than formal apprenticeship. Combat is structurally safe (sparring automatically stops around half health), and disconnected players are preserved in place rather than swept into a holding room.

libs.name: Dead Souls 3.8.6
libs.english_description: The classic, widely-deployed "Dead Souls" LPC mudlib base (v3.8.6, released 2014), descended from Descartes of Borg's Nightmare mudlib. Unlike every other lib in this collection, Dead Souls isn't a themed game in its own right -- it's a generic, well-documented starter codebase that hundreds of real-world LPMuds have been built on top of, shipped here close to stock. A fresh boot runs its own first-time admin installation wizard (register the admin's name/password/gender, then the driver restarts itself), after which the world is the small stock demo area: a campus, a scripted line editor (ed/qed), a bulletin board, mail, an in-game creation system for builders, and a starter "Players Handbook" new characters are pointed at on login.

libs.name: DTSL
libs.english_name: Twin Dragons of the Tang Dynasty
libs.english_description: Based on Huang Yi's wuxia novel of the same name and set in the turbulent jianghu of the early Tang dynasty. One of three independently developed games in this project (alongside dtsl2 and dtslmud) that share part of a base engine while each builds its own storyline. New characters begin at the Great Tang Academy, where a guided curriculum introduces the basics before players head down the mountain into the wider world.

libs.name: 大唐双龙传（LLMUD）
libs.english_name: Twin Dragons of the Tang Dynasty (LLMUD)
libs.english_description: LLMUD v0.11, adapted from Huang Yi's novel "Twin Dragons of the Tang Dynasty" and a sister build sharing the same underlying architecture as dtsl. Set at the fall of the Sui dynasty and the rise of Tang, players start at the Great Tang Academy and grow through four core attributes assigned at registration, joining sects and factions amid a jianghu of rival warlords; wizards and admins carry the in-game title "Heavenly Emperor."

libs.name: 大唐双龙 (DaTangShuangLong)
libs.english_name: Twin Dragons of the Tang Dynasty (DaTangShuangLong)
libs.english_description: Another independent implementation in this project's "Twin Dragons of the Tang Dynasty" family (alongside dtsl and dtslmud), based on Huang Yi's novel and set amid the chaos of the early Tang jianghu. Shares some base items and Chinese-name validation logic with its siblings but is built on its own codebase; new characters start at the Great Tang Academy and the Stone Dragon Martial Hall, a beginner hub offering banking, apprenticeship, and NPC sparring.

libs.name: 东方故事（蓝天） — es1_win
libs.english_description: An early foundational build of the "Eastern Story" series and part of the ES/TMI engine family — despite the wuxia-sounding name, it's actually a Western-style fantasy world in the D&D tradition. Shares its core engine with esI (this project's "Dragon Slaying War" build). Offers over a dozen playable races (humans, elves, dwarves, orcs, goblins, halflings, lizardfolk, and more) and a guild-based, rather than sect-based, system of knightly orders, mage towers, priesthoods, monasteries, and thieves' guilds.

libs.name: 东方故事 — esI（"屠龙之战"）
libs.english_description: Another build of "Eastern Story," themed around an in-game event called the Dragon Slaying War. Shares nearly identical core code with es1_win (Eastern Story: Blue Sky) from this same engine family, differing mainly in site content and branch details. This particular snapshot ships with a test-era configuration that grants new characters automatic wizard privileges, suggesting it was originally used for internal testing or load trials rather than public play.

libs.name: 风云Ⅳ — fengyun434
libs.english_description: Produced by Sumxin's Fengyun studio, part of this project's "Fengyun" wuxia engine family shared with fy2, fy2005, fy2qh, fy3xd, and fy3dz — each a separate content branch from a different site or era built on the same core engine. Set in a jianghu drawn from Gu Long's wuxia novels, players begin as an ordinary commoner just entering the martial world, choosing an ethnicity (Han, Miao, Manchu, or Mongol) that shapes starting attributes and birthplace.

libs.name: 风云Ⅳ（2005 国内经典版）— fy2005
libs.english_description: The same "Fengyun IV" engine as fengyun434, captured as a different year/site snapshot, with identical Gu Long-inspired wuxia gameplay of choosing an ethnic background and making one's way through jianghu sects. Notable for an ASCII-art CAPTCHA at registration — an unusually early anti-bot measure for this engine family — and for only persisting characters who reach at least 40% experience toward level 2.

libs.name: 西游记 (A Journey to the West)
libs.english_description: Self-titled "A Journey to the West," version 2.01, originally created 1996-1998. This project's research concludes it is very likely the earliest ancestor of the entire "ES II / Journey to the West" engine family (which includes xyj2000f, mhxy, xiyouji2003, xiyouji2006, xiyouji450, shenmo, and other sibling games in this collection) — its files carry the earliest timestamps and show none of the "cracker" credit lines later sites added. Set in the world of the original novel, players set out from Chang'an to explore the story's iconic locations (the Silk-Web Cave, Five-Finger Mountain, the South Sea, and more). As the wellspring of the whole Journey to the West MUD lineage its world content is comparatively simple, the most primitive form in the series and a useful baseline for comparing how the later branches evolved.

libs.name: 西游记 2000 — xyj2000f
libs.english_name: Journey to the West: New Era
libs.english_description: Journey to the West: New Era (xiyouji.org), a classic old-school MUD from the late 1990s. Part of the Eastern Tale (ES) / Journey to the West engine family, sharing lineage with this project's other "Journey to the West" titles.

libs.name: 西游记[光辉岁月]
libs.english_name: Journey to the West: Glory Days
libs.english_description: A circa-2003 entry in the Journey to the West series of text MUDs, part of the same "ES II / Journey to the West" family as this project's xyj2000f, xiyouji, xiyouji2006, xiyouji450, and mhxy — its core engine code (master.c) is nearly identical to xyj2000f, making it a later, more content-rich offshoot of that branch. Players set out from the South City Inn in Chang'an to face "eighty-one trials" across the three realms of heaven, earth, and the underworld, backed by a fairly developed system of sects, guilds, warfare, marriage, and Five Elements attributes. The inn's message board still preserves genuine historical developer announcements — quest-system revision notes, bug-fix notices, sect leaderboard rules — a firsthand record of how the site was run at the time.

libs.name: 西游记450
libs.english_description: A distribution package built specifically for setting up "mirror sites," complete with a tutorial for other site operators to launch their own branch on top of it. It belongs to the same closely related "Journey to the West / xiyouji.org" engine family as this project's xyj2000f, mhxy, and mhxyqd — its core engine files (master.c, chinese.c, and others) are nearly word-for-word identical to mhxy, differing only in the site's own login/security layer and world content. Set in the Journey to the West universe, players start at the South City Inn in Chang'an and explore the three realms while practicing martial arts and joining sects; as a mirror-site package its world closely resembles the xyj2000f/mhxy line but runs its own independent registration and security system.

libs.archive: 西游记2006之 最终幻想.rar
libs.name: 西游记2006·大唐西游
libs.english_name: Journey to the West 2006: Great Tang Pilgrimage
libs.english_description: Its saved files carry three different names: the archive is labeled "Final Fantasy," the login banner announces itself as "Journey to the West 2006: The Final Madness," and in-game notices declare it formally renamed to Great Tang Journey West. Part of the mhxy/Dream of Journey to the West engine family, sharing common ancestry with this project's mhxy and shenmo (Journey to the West: Legend of Gods and Demons) but independently developed and maintained by a different site for years, with substantially diverged content. Players alternate between growing as an ordinary mortal (apprenticing under a master, building a life) and following two signature storylines, "the journey west" and "havoc in heaven," with leaderboards for wealth, kills, and cultivation, and the Tang Monk and his disciples wandering the map as background NPCs to reinforce the atmosphere.

libs.name: 风云再起Ⅱ — fy2
libs.english_description: Developed by the Computer and Information Engineering College of Hohai University, part of this project's "Fengyun" wuxia engine family alongside fy2005, fengyun434, fy3xd, and fy3dz. Set in a jianghu drawn from Gu Long's wuxia novels, new players choose an ethnicity and start out at the Fengqiuhuang Inn or Chenxiang Town as a novice adventurer; the nearby "Money Gang" offers newcomers an easy first apprenticeship, and two long-running message boards preserve years of player-written poems and reflections.

libs.name: 风云II
libs.english_description: File-by-file comparison confirms this archive is actually another surviving copy of the same source code as the sibling game fy2 (differing only in bundled driver and player-save snapshot) — the “Tsinghua remake” label looks like a name a download or mirror site gave this particular copy at the time, rather than an independent rewrite. The content is identical to fy2: a Gu Long-style wuxia world where players can join the beginner-friendly Money Gang, browse the Fengyun Square message board and the Poetry Terrace, and use a full set of emotes.

libs.name: 梦幻西游 (mhxy)
libs.english_description: Running as the "Qingdao Station" branch since January 15, 2002, part of the classic Journey to the West-themed engine family (sharing lineage with this project's xyj2000f, among others), built on a MudOS V22Pre11-labeled core.

libs.name: 梦幻西游（青岛站）
libs.english_description: A 2002 release under the "Qingdao Station" branch — the same 2002 codebase as this project's mhxy archive (differing only in station branding), part of the Journey to the West-themed ES II engine family shared with xyj2000f, among others.

libs.name: 侠客行 (MUD侠客行2017完整版)
libs.english_name: Xia Ke Xing — 2017 Complete Edition (Ode to Gallantry)
libs.english_description: Based on Jin Yong's novel Ode to Gallantry (Xia Ke Xing), this archive is labeled the "2017 Complete Edition." It shares its name with this collection's xiakexing100 and xiakexing3, but its codebase is entirely independent — the core engine files differ across all three. New characters start at an inn and can train in martial arts, meet fellow wanderers, and join the major sects, while the game clock displays "Xia Ke Xing time," real Beijing time, and the lunar calendar side by side.

libs.name: 仙剑奇侠传 (nitan170911)
libs.english_description: The largest of the 'nitan' (NT/Lonely) engine family games in this collection, weighing in at roughly 54,000 files. Set in the world of the beloved Chinese Paladin / Sword and Fairy (Xianjian Qixia Zhuan) game and TV franchise, it shares its core attribute-storage architecture with its smaller sibling nitan6 (Laughing in the Wind). Its account system depends on an external MySQL server for cross-site character syncing, so in this archived environment new registration is gracefully declined rather than broken — it's best explored by browsing the code and world content rather than played start to finish.

libs.name: 洪荒世界
libs.english_description: Sourced from a “Primordial World (Self-Connecting Database)” archive within a 2026-07-29 batch upload. A member of the NT/nitan/Lonely engine family — related to nitan170911 (Chinese Paladin) and nitan6 (Laughing in the Wind) in this project — redesigned here around the world of Investiture of the Gods and the myth of Pangu separating heaven and earth.

libs.name: 洪荒世界（修复版）
libs.english_name: Honghuang World — Fixed Edition (World of Primordial Chaos)
libs.english_description: Part of the "Nitan" (NT) mudlib lineage, sharing a byte-identical master codebase with this collection's hhsj (the original Honghuang World) and nitan170911. New characters begin in the "Nitan Registration Hall" and must complete an elaborate, multi-step "birth" ritual — choosing a race, gender, and temperament, then allocating attribute points in the "Valley of Life" — before truly entering the world.

libs.name: 笑傲江湖 (nitan6)
libs.english_description: One of the two largest 'nitan' (NT/Lonely) engine games in this collection, at over 23,000 files, based on Jin Yong's classic wuxia novel The Smiling, Proud Wanderer. Characters are reincarnated from the Valley of Life into a full Jin-Yong-style jianghu of sects — Sun Moon Sect, Mount Hua, Shaolin, the Beggars' Sect, and more — building up internal power, lightness kung fu, fist skills, and weapon mastery, with gang prestige, military merit, marriage, and mounts all fleshed out. The Beggars' Sect even has its own quirky tree-hollow initiation ritual, and a one-shot 'wash' command lets players fully re-roll their starting attributes.

libs.name: 大唐西游 YWX人造人 (rzrmud)
libs.english_description: A North America-hosted Journey to the West game, self-branded 'YWX Cyborg' after its original developer/team, continuously running since February 2006 with over five hundred registered player accounts on record — among the most solidly 'actually operated' archives in this collection. It shares its mythic Journey to the West setting with sibling game mhxy but runs on an independently engineered codebase, with per-object attribute accessors rather than the shared global-store architecture common to the nitan/Lonely family. New characters begin at the South City Inn in Chang'an, greeted by classic characters like Bai Suzhen and Tang Sanzang, and follow a cultivation-focused progression built around sects, Five Elements attack/defense attributes, and Taoist cultivation realms, with a fairly generous newbie starter-kit system.

libs.name: 侠客行 Ⅰ (The Quest of Oriental Chivalry)
libs.english_description: Produced by the "XiaKeXing Gaming Group," with a login screen claiming a 1996-2003 pedigree. Part of an early branch of the ES II engine family, sharing a more distant common technical ancestry with this project's rzrmud (Great Tang Journey West), bmxkx2001, and xuanjianlu (Record of the Mysterious Sword), though each has an independent game world — at the release level, scene files such as d/taihu/gumu/houtang.lpc carry the "Cracked by Roath" header shared with bmxkx2001/jym/xkm, while xuanjianlu belongs to a separate "Cracked by Kafei" batch (shared with xkx2000zxb); the two batches differ in header credit but share the same core engine. Set on "Xiake Island," new characters wake on the island's beach and are greeted by the "Rewarding Envoy" Zhang San or the "Punishing Envoy" Li Si, who guide them to registration before they set out into the jianghu proper. The world covers classic Jin Yong sects — Shaolin, Wudang, Huashan, the Beggars' Sect, the Xiuzhong Sect, and more — with a full apprenticeship, inner-cultivation, quest, and clan system; new arrivals must first follow a welcoming NPC to the island's registry and complete `register <email>`, a vintage anti-multi-accounting mechanism from the era.

libs.name: 侠客行 (The Quest of Oriental Chivalry) — 北美 2001 版
libs.english_name: The Quest of Oriental Chivalry (North American 2001 Edition)
libs.english_description: Based on Jin Yong's wuxia novel of the same name and centered on Xiake Island, where new players are greeted by one of the island's two envoys and led through registration before entering the wider jianghu. Part of the ES II / "Xiake Xing" engine family, this is a North American release circulated by the XiaKeXing Gaming Group in the late 1990s, with a faithful sect and martial-arts system and an unusually detailed death-and-resurrection sequence.

libs.name: 新仙侣情缘之飘渺纪元
libs.english_name: New Immortal Companions' Bond: Age of Mist
libs.english_description: Part of the ES II engine family and the same lineage as "Immortal Companions' Bond (Early Test Build)" (xlqy_early) — a more complete and mature version of the same codebase, subtitled "Station of Chaos."

libs.name: 仙侣情缘（早期测试版）
libs.english_description: Part of the ES II engine family and the same lineage as its sibling archive "New Immortal Companions' Bond: Age of Mist" (xlqy_new2007) — an earlier, rougher development snapshot of the same codebase. According to notes included in the archive itself, it was originally a half-finished build the author used to test driver compatibility.

libs.name: 仙侣情缘·浙大版
libs.english_name: Immortal Companions' Bond: Zhejiang University Edition
libs.english_description: Developed by bugbug and alading as a second-generation build on top of the "Misty Waters" server. An independent branch within the Immortal Companions' Bond (XLQY) engine family — distinct from this archive's other Immortal Companions' Bond codebase (the 2001 Zhiqiu-station version), though they share the same core engine.

libs.name: 笑傲江湖（迷你版）
libs.english_description: Part of the TMI-2/ES2 ("Falcon") engine family, and the smallest, most minimal build in the Smiling, Proud Wanderer series — the author's own "mini xo." Its sibling archive, the Final Edition (xo_final), was expanded directly from this mini version.

libs.name: 笑傲江湖（最终版）
libs.english_description: Part of the TMI-2/ES2 ("Falcon") engine family, greatly expanded from the Mini Edition (xo). The author describes it as their own private test server, with several times the content of the mini build.

libs.name: 笑傲江湖 II
libs.english_name: The Smiling, Proud Wanderer II (Xiao Ao Jiang Hu II)
libs.english_description: The login screen calls this game "Virtual Life." It belongs to the "XO mudlib" engine family (descended from TMI-2/ES2, rewritten by "Falcon" in 1996), sharing lineage with this collection's Xiao Ao Jiang Hu Mini Edition and XO Final 1.2, but is an independent, later snapshot of the game — in-game notices show it opened on April 1, 2003.

libs.name: 笑傲江湖 XO
libs.english_name: Xiao Ao Jiang Hu XO (The Smiling, Proud Wanderer)
libs.english_description: Based on Jin Yong's novel The Smiling, Proud Wanderer, "XO" is this version's own codename (the login banner reads "THE SMILING PROUD WANDERER"), descended from the TMI-2/ES2 engine lineage and rewritten by "Falcon." This collection also holds two other snapshots of the same bloodline, xo (Mini Edition) and xo_final (Final 1.2); this archive is the third, independently evolved branch of the three.

libs.name: 清华笑傲江湖
libs.english_description: A Tsinghua University take on Jin Yong's The Smiling, Proud Wanderer, sharing the TMI-2/ES2/Falcon engine family with sibling games xo and xo_final in this collection but built with independently developed sects and story content, centered on the 'Nanyang' region map and noticeably more compact than the xo series. New character names are filtered against a blocklist of Jin Yong novel character names, so players can't register as the original book's own protagonists. Combat writing is unusually detailed, with distinct flavor text for hits, parries, and dodges.

libs.name: 郑州风云3
libs.english_description: Introduces itself in-game as 'Invincible Under Heaven' (the collector-assigned title 'Zhengzhou Storm 3' names this particular server instance). Part of the Fengyun ('Storm') engine family, alongside this collection's fy2/fy2005/fengyun434/moniHuafu. The game bills itself as 'a MUD set in the world of Gu Long's novels' — rather than the Jin Yong-flavored wuxia common elsewhere in this collection, it leans into Gu Long's brisk, devil-may-care style of jianghu storytelling. Character creation lets players choose an ethnicity (Han, Miao, Manchu, or Mongol), an unusual touch for this engine family.

libs.name: 风云III修订版
libs.english_description: The readme bundled with the original archive calls this “Storm III, revised by Xingxing” — a content-rich version compiled and revised by a community enthusiast going by “Xingxing.” It belongs to this batch's Fengyun III (Storm III) engine branch, sharing highly similar core code with fy3dz (the “Storm Collector's Edition”) — a different content package built on the same engine.

libs.name: 风云III典藏版
libs.english_description: Storm 3.8.0, a “collector's edition” compiled internally by the “Storm Studio” team, building on Storm 3.7.4 with previously unreleased or otherwise lost original content. It belongs to this batch's Fengyun III (Storm III) engine branch — its core engine code is nearly identical to fy3xd (the “Xingxing revision”) — and is one of the most content-complete packages in that branch.

libs.name: 世纪
libs.english_description: Self-titled "Century" (rendered as CENTURY in the login banner's copyright notice, which carries the tagline "Star Wars Heroes in a World of Chaos and Dust"). Built on the adm/single/{master,simul_efun} layout, it shares a common lineage with several sibling "Century family" sites elsewhere in this archive.

libs.name: 东方故事二
libs.english_name: Eastern Story II: The Celestial Empire
libs.english_description: Part of the "Eastern Story" engine family shared with es1_win and esI in this project, but with independent, smaller-scale content — an early MUD established in 1995-1996. Offers four playable races (Human, Jiaojao, Woochan, Yenhold) drawing more on Western fantasy than wuxia sect traditions, with new characters beginning at a small inn greeted by an innkeeper and waiter in a leaner, old-school style typical of this engine family.

libs.name: 中华英雄苏州站
libs.english_description: The full login banner reads 'China Hero II: Wuxia World' — this archive is the 'Suzhou Station' server instance, which opened on March 1, 2006. Its core engine is a derivative branch of the ES II engine family (the master file's authorship trail runs from 'Lil' through 'Annihilator' and 'Xiang for XKX' to 'Doing Lu for hell', before being rewritten by 'Linux@lxtx'). It shares a distant common ancestor with this collection's other 'Ultimate Hell'/'Xuanyuan Legend' titles, but its content and gameplay have diverged into a relatively independent branch.

libs.name: 书剑天下 2008
libs.english_description: A 2008 build made by the ShuJian MUD development team and hosted by Chongqing Telecom. Its source is nearly identical to the similarly named sjtx2 (Little Bear branch) elsewhere in this archive — two independent deployments of the same game on different sites.

libs.name: 书剑天下（小熊泥苑分站）
libs.english_name: Book and Sword Under Heaven (Little Bear Branch)
libs.english_description: Self-titled "Book and Sword Under Heaven," like shujian2008, this is a branch deployed by the "Little Bear Mud Garden" (dtxy.126.com) site. Its source is nearly identical to shujian2008's — two independent deployments of the same game on different servers.

libs.name: 书剑飘零Ⅱ
libs.english_description: Self-titled "Stray Book & Sword," made by Feibai Studio. Despite sharing the words "Book and Sword" in its name, it is a completely separate, unrelated codebase from shujian2008 and sjtx2 elsewhere in this archive.

libs.name: 仙侣情缘（知秋站 2001版）
libs.english_description: A 2001 snapshot from the "Zhiqiu" site (www.mudfan.com), part of the Fairy Love Story engine family and a sibling to this project's separately archived "Zhejiang University edition" branch, but with earlier code closer to the original. In-game it calls itself "A Journey to the West: Fairy Love Story." Players set out from an inn in southern Chang'an and cultivate through stages of the Tao, martial arts, and inner power toward a scripture-seeking, havoc-in-heaven-style story arc, with an overall casual pace.

libs.name: 仙剑狂侠2000（仙剑传奇）
libs.english_name: Immortal Sword Wandering Knight 2000 (Legend of the Sword)
libs.english_description: By author Ye Yufei. Part of the "Century" family of wuxia MUD engines (sharing lineage with Book and Sword 2008 and Book and Sword: Adrift II, with similar admin directory structures), though its game content and security modules were independently developed rather than copied. Set in a traditional wuxia world centered on Yangzhou — its central square, shops, the provincial governor's office, and major sects (the Beggars' Sect, Quanzhen Sect, White Camel Mountain, the Five Poisons Sect, the Sun Moon Holy Cult, and more). Distinctive "banditry" and "armed escort" job systems add flavor to jianghu life, all in an orthodox Jin Yong/Gu Long-style wuxia atmosphere well suited to players who enjoy sect progression and quest systems.

libs.name: 侠客新传 (New Legend of the Wandering Swordsman)
libs.english_name: New Legend of the Wandering Swordsman
libs.english_description: A wuxia mudlib developed by the "Xkxz MUD Wizard Group." A leftover "Ocean II Shanghai Main Site" field in its config file suggests the code was likely built as a second-generation development on top of the "Ocean II" engine, though the actual game content and login banner present it as an independent title. The game opens at a "Peach Blossom Spring" paradise-like starting scene and blends character archetypes (Warrior, Wisdom, Endurance, Agility, Balanced) with sect martial arts for its wuxia progression system. Distinctively, a new character does not immediately "reincarnate" after basic registration — players must find the NPC Shuisheng in-game and complete `register <email>` before choosing their aptitude and gaining full stats, an intentional onboarding design rather than a bug.

libs.name: 侠客英雄传 III
libs.english_name: Legend of the Chivalrous Hero III
libs.english_description: A small, independently built wuxia MUD running on an early home-grown domestic MudOS engine (with the classic adm/obj directory layout). It doesn't belong to any larger game lineage in this archive — a standalone, compact creation with its own codebase.

libs.name: 侠客行一百 (Xia Ke Xing - Yi Bai)
libs.english_name: Xia Ke Xing 100 (Ode to Gallantry — Centennial Edition)
libs.english_description: Based on Jin Yong's novel Ode to Gallantry (Xia Ke Xing), developed since 2001 by author Coollizard and the xkx100 team. It belongs to this collection's "Century" mudlib family (built around an adm/single/ directory layout) and is the largest of that group by file count — roughly 12,000 LPC files after conversion. Its map is built around real historical Chinese cities, including Beijing, Chang'an, Luoyang, and Yangzhou, with new characters starting at a randomly assigned home-city inn.

libs.name: 金庸群侠传（2008 加强版）
libs.english_name: Legend of Jin Yong's Heroes (2008 Enhanced Edition)
libs.english_description: Self-titled "Legend of Jin Yong's Heroes," this archive corresponds to the "2008 Enhanced" content release. It's an independent branch of the "ES II" engine family (tracing to author Phoebus.suny's 1998 ES2 "Heavenly Court, Earthly Realm" release); this project also holds other content releases built on the same engine core (Standard, Deluxe, and 2015 editions) — essentially the same server program with different content configurations.

libs.name: 金庸群侠传（2008 标准版）
libs.english_name: Legend of Jin Yong's Heroes (2008 Standard Edition)
libs.english_description: This archive corresponds to the base "2008" (Standard) content release, sharing an identical server engine core with this project's "2008 Enhanced" edition (the master, login, and security modules match byte for byte), with only somewhat fewer quests and lighter scene descriptions than the Enhanced edition.

libs.name: 金庸群侠传（2008 超豪华版）
libs.english_name: Legend of Jin Yong's Heroes (2008 Deluxe Edition)
libs.english_description: This archive corresponds to the "2008 Deluxe" content release, sharing an identical server engine core with this project's "2008 Enhanced" and "2008 Standard" editions, but with its own adjustments to sect NPCs, combat numbers, and some map scenes — and the largest file size of the three.

libs.name: 金庸群侠传（2015版）
libs.english_name: Legend of Jin Yong's Heroes (2015 Edition)
libs.english_description: A version compiled and released in 2015, part of the ES II engine series — sharing the same underlying engine/daemon code with this project's "2008 Enhanced" edition and its siblings. The engine itself changed little over those seven years; what changed was the content, with this edition adding a number of new areas and storylines beyond the 2008 release.

libs.name: 金庸群侠传 (原名"侠客行三")
libs.english_name: Heroes of Jin Yong (formerly Xia Ke Xing III)
libs.english_description: Both the archive and its internal config call this game "Xia Ke Xing III," but the actual login banner reads "Heroes of Jin Yong" (Jin Yong Qun Xia Zhuan). It shares its core master codebase with this collection's jqxz2008 series — a different-era reskin and content version of the same engine. Deeper functional testing later corrected an overly optimistic early assessment, uncovering and fixing several real bugs, including a broken food/water initialization check and a crash affecting all 18 bulletin boards in the game.

libs.name: 夕阳再现-疯狂江湖
libs.english_description: The site's subtitle is "Crazy Jianghu." It belongs to the Sunset Reappears family of wuxia MUD engines, sharing common roots with this project's xyzxfy2 (Storm Rises Again II), wmkj, jhfy, and bixiecanyang — each an independent game world built by a different site on the same base engine. This branch carries the genuine Sunset Reappears map lineage (byte-identical to xyzx, jhfy3, xajh4gkb, and xyzxyl201412), unlike another cluster of archives in this collection that share the same branding but actually run on an unrelated "Tianya" map family.

libs.name: 夕阳再现·风云再起Ⅱ
libs.english_name: Sunset Reappears: Storm Rises Again II
libs.english_description: The site's subtitle is "Storm Rises Again II" (domain www.zhaoshu.net). It belongs to the same Sunset Reappears family of wuxia MUD engines as this project's xyzxfk (Crazy Jianghu) — the two share some underlying files, but their login, security, and world content were developed independently as two separate games built on a common engine. This branch carries the genuine Sunset Reappears map lineage (byte-identical to xyzx, jhfy3, xajh4gkb, and xyzxyl201412), unlike another cluster of similarly-branded archives in this collection whose maps actually belong to an unrelated "Tianya" family.

libs.name: 江湖风云
libs.english_description: The game calls itself Jianghu Storm: Single-Player Edition. Core-file comparison against two related titles in this project (Sunset Reappears: Frenzied Jianghu, and Unknown Space) confirms all three descend from the same lineage — the “Sunset Reappears: Jianghu Storm” branch of Chinese wuxia MUDs — with this version standing closest to their common ancestor, making it the core release of the series. This is the same true “Sunset Reappears” lineage as xyzx, jhfy3, xajh4gkb, and xyzxyl201412 handled elsewhere in this project; note that a separate, unrelated “Tianya” family of archives (xysylmhb, xyzxiiylzymh, yzxiiizylfy, xyzx3, etc.) also carries “Sunset Reappears” branding despite having an entirely different map — the brand name alone isn't a reliable lineage signal.

libs.name: 夕阳再现III之炎龙封印
libs.english_name: Sunset Reappears III: Seal of the Fire Dragon
libs.english_description: The full title is "Sunset Reappears III: Seal of the Fire Dragon," made in 2006 by AKAI Studio; the actual site name shown on login is "Jianghu Storm." It's a representative example of classic domestic MudOS wuxia MUDs, built around traditional sects and internal-power cultivation. This archive is nearly identical to the sibling archive xysylmhb — matching .lpc file counts, directory structure, and map content — and was likely split from the same original package into two separate archives here; its map actually belongs to the unrelated "Tianya" lineage rather than the true Sunset Reappears bloodline, a reminder that shared branding doesn't reliably indicate shared code in this batch of games.

libs.archive: 炎龙封印-笑傲江湖3阿飞站.rar
libs.name: 炎龙封印（笑傲江湖·阿飞站）
libs.english_name: Seal of the Fire Dragon (Laughing in the Wind: Afei's Server)
libs.english_description: Belongs to the Sunset Reappears (XYZX/YLFY) engine family; its in-game login banner reads "Sunset Reappears: Laughing in the Wind." This build is a deep independent reworking by developer "Afei," built atop an earlier Fire Dragon branch modified by "Suimeng" — making it a distant cousin, rather than a direct copy, of the other Sunset Reappears games in this collection's engine family.

libs.archive: 龙云梦-炎龙封印源码版.rar
libs.name: 龙云梦·炎龙封印（源码版）
libs.english_name: Dragon Cloud Dream: Flame Dragon Seal (Source Edition)
libs.english_description: By author Wenwu, an independent branch within the "Sunset Reappears / Flame Dragon Seal" (XYZX/YLFY) engine family — related to but separately evolved from this project's ylfyxa3 (Flame Dragon Seal: Smiling Proud Wanderer, Afei Station), not a reskin of the same content. It shares the genuine "Sunset Reappears" code lineage (a byte-identical d/city/sj.lpc) with xyzx, jhfy3, xajh4gkb, and xyzxyl201412; note that several other archives in this project also carry the "Sunset Reappears" brand but belong to an entirely different "Tianya" map lineage, so the brand name alone is not a reliable guide to actual codebase ancestry.

libs.archive: 龙云梦-炎龙封印-二进制版.rar
libs.name: 龙云梦·炎龙封印（二进制版）
