libs.archive: lpmuds.net/files/tmi2_fluffos_v3.zip, recovered via Wayback Machine 2026-08-25 (original site down)
libs.name: TMI-2
libs.english_description: A historically significant, widely-copied English-language LPMud mudlib from 1992-1996 whose std/ base classes, command-soul dispatch, and /adm/-rooted security-daemon layout were inherited by a large family of later mudlibs (this project's own catalog refers to a 'TMI-2/Falcon family' of descendants). This port is the 'famous TMI-2 quad' release: a landing zone with a bulletin board and discussion rooms, the full wizard toolset, and character creation across 13 playable races. The most severe porting bug: master.lpc's domain_file() crashed with an uncaught array-index-out-of-bounds error on the driver's own first boot-time call, because this driver's SANE_EXPLODE_STRING build returns an empty array from explode('/','/') where old-style MudOS returned a two-element one -- the existing null-check never covered the empty case, and the failure happened so early in boot that the top-level error message gave no indication of the real cause. A second bug: two live-loaded files (the channel daemon and the wizard reference-variable daemon) used 'ref' as an ordinary identifier, a name this driver reserves as a pass-by-reference keyword.

libs.archive: lpmuds.net/files/foundation/foundation2_fluffos_v1.zip, recovered via Wayback Machine 2026-08-25 (original site down)
libs.name: Foundation II
libs.english_description: A stripped-down classic descendant of the Nightmare mudlib lineage from the mid-1990s, positioned by its own boot banner as an engine for hardcore LPC programmers, not a beginner-friendly game world -- it ships no combat, limbs, or stats system at all. What shipped and works: a real first-boot admin-setup installation wizard, full login/registration, security/privs access control, command dispatch, help, mail, message boards, and Intermud-3 networking, plus one small starting domain. Porting it surfaced two especially wide-reaching FluffOS-compat bugs: a missing creator_file() master apply (required by this driver's PACKAGE_UIDS support on every single object load) broke loading almost the entire mudlib, and a .c-to-.lpc rename side effect in the command-dispatch table's filename parsing silently broke every ordinary player/wizard command while soul/emote commands kept working through a separate path. Two optional example/teaching content trees included in the archive reference an incompatible, differently-named room/item API from a different snapshot of this engine and don't compile -- a pre-existing content mismatch, not fixed.

libs.archive: lpmuds.net/files/skylib_fluffos_v3.zip, recovered via Wayback Machine 2026-08-25 (original site down)
libs.name: Skylib
libs.english_description: Version 1.8 of Skylib, an English-language LPMud library in the Discworld/Nightmare lineage (boot banner: "Divided Sky Distribution Lib"), built around the same soul/directory-based command dispatch as Discworld rather than the driver's native add_action(). Porting it surfaced two especially wide-reaching FluffOS-compat bugs beyond the usual .c-to-.lpc rename side effects (found in 11 files, not just __FILE__ comparisons): the archive's own bundled include/runtime_config.h used a stale, mismatched get_config() index numbering that silently returned wrong-typed values instead of erroring, and -- the big one -- this driver build compiles WITH native add_action() support, which this mudlib barely uses, so its own command-dispatch fallback into the real command() efun always failed silently and its process_input() apply always told the driver "unhandled," causing every single typed command to be swallowed and doubly rejected with "What?" before the mudlib's real directory-based dispatcher (cmdAll/new_parser/lower_check) ever ran. Fixed with a small set of #if efun_defined(add_action)-gated compat shims. What works after fixing: full registration, login, and the real player command set (look/score/inventory/quit and more), verified live. A first-boot "creator only mode" lockdown (this lib's own safety default on any fresh install) required a save-file edit to open registration and to seed the project's admin account into the archive's own placeholder admin-group entry. Roughly 127 of 2163 files still fail lpcc's standalone compile sweep, almost all pre-existing content gaps predating this port (deliberately-broken LPC-error teaching examples, master.lpc mixins that only compile as part of the whole object, a dead/superseded alternate room-topography system, obsolete std/guilds/old/* content calling a set_race() function that was renamed/removed mudlib-wide, missing marry.h/rituals.h headers, and one file shipped in the original archive itself as a single line with zero newlines) -- logged in NOTES.md, not fixed, per this project's content-vs-driver-compat scope. Like imud/foundation2, this lib makes a real outbound Intermud-3 socket connection at boot (to a near-certainly-defunct 1990s host) and should not be swept into high-frequency automated re-boot loops.

libs.archive: lpmuds.net/files/merentha_fluffos_v2.zip, recovered via Wayback Machine 2026-08-25 (original site down)
libs.name: Merentha
libs.english_description: A classic English-language LPMud lib explicitly based on the popular Nightmare 3 lib, per its own description aiming to have "the Nightmare feel and robustness without the complications of verbs or weird lfun names." New characters wake in a race-selection limbo room (a wall of frozen male/female bodies in wall compartments, one pair per race), pick a gender and race with `become <gender> <race>` from six options (human, giant, gnome, elf, dwarf, fairy), and land in the Cabeiri starting town with its central square, guild halls (fighter/mage/healer/monk), and general supply shop. Ships a full skill-point system (30+ skills from swordplay to alchemy to bargaining), a limb-based body model, an Intermud-3 daemon, and a wizard-oriented `/cmds/admin` toolset. Porting it surfaced one real driver-compat blocker: this driver's PACKAGE_UIDS support requires get_root_uid()/get_bb_uid() master-object applies that this archive never defined at all (the driver refuses to boot past master-object load without them) -- fixed by porting the same two-line pair used by the closely-related nightmare3 lib in this collection. Everything else in the ~140-file mudlib compiled and ran clean on the first pass.

libs.name: Discworld MUD lib (v3)
libs.english_description: The official Discworld MUD's mudlib, as redistributed by Cratylus (Dead Souls' maintainer) in a self-contained "Discworld Bundle" paired with a matching FluffOS build (dw_fluffos_v3 is the latest of three snapshots this project holds; v1/v2 are kept as unconverted alternate archives). One of the longest-running, most-studied LPMuds in existence (running continuously since 1991), set in Terry Pratchett's Discworld. New characters start in the famous circular Discworld Room in Ankh-Morpork's Cabbage Warehouse Rooming House, guided in by a wandering "womble" NPC. Uses a directory-based command dispatcher (a verb like `look` resolves to a file `cmds/living/l_ook.lpc`, the underscore marking its minimum abbreviation) layered under a `drunk_check()`/`lower_check()` eval-cost and command-queueing throttle -- both mechanisms register as add_action catch-alls, which on this project's FluffOS build required the verb "" instead of the codebase's original "*" convention (see NOTES.md).
